semantic_correction.stem: A client admitted with an acute ischemic stroke asks for water and has oral medications due. The client is awake and can follow commands, but the facility-approved dysphagia screen has not yet been completed. Which action is most appropriate?

options.A: Give several small sips of water while the client sits upright, then stop oral intake only if coughing or a wet voice develops.
options.B: Keep the client NPO, including oral medications, and complete the facility-approved dysphagia screening process before oral intake.
options.C: Offer thickened liquids instead of water until a speech-language pathologist can evaluate swallowing later in the hospitalization.
options.D: Administer oral medications crushed in applesauce because medication doses should not be delayed while the swallow screen is pending.

semantic_correction.rationale: The 2026 NCSBN NCLEX-RN Test Plan explicitly includes identifying clients at risk for aspiration, including those with swallowing difficulties, and intervening to prevent aspiration under Reduction of Risk Potential. The 2026 American Heart Association/American Stroke Association acute ischemic stroke guideline states that dysphagia screening before initiating oral intake may identify patients at risk and guide safe nutritional management. Current AHA stroke-quality criteria operationalize this by measuring whether stroke patients undergo an evidence-based dysphagia screen before receiving food, fluids, or medications by mouth, or remain NPO. Because this client has acute stroke and the approved screening process is still pending, B is the uniquely safest response: do not give water, food, or oral medications until swallowing safety is assessed according to the facility process. A uses oral water itself before screening and may miss silent aspiration. C assumes thickened liquid is safe before swallowing assessment. D gives oral medication in food before swallowing safety has been established. Therefore B is correct.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: After acute stroke, prevent aspiration by withholding oral food, fluids, and medications until swallowing safety has been assessed through the approved dysphagia-screening process rather than testing swallowing informally or assuming a modified texture is safe.
semantic_correction.source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN); American Heart Association/American Stroke Association (AHA/ASA)

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: retired generic multigenerational-teamwork/stereotype recall because it was managerial and the correct response had an extreme length cue. Rebuilt the item around explicit NCSBN aspiration-risk/prevention content and current 2026 AHA/ASA stroke guidance. The final item requires withholding oral intake until the approved dysphagia-screening process is completed and removes the prior answer-length cue.

audit_findings_append.finding: The replacement directly tests prevention of aspiration after acute stroke before swallowing safety has been established.

scope_exclusions.specific_swallow_screen_tool: Not prescribed. The stem refers to the facility-approved process because screening tools and qualified screeners vary by organization.
scope_exclusions.automatic_SLP_evaluation_for_every_strok: Not asserted. The item requires the approved initial swallowing-safety screening process; further specialist evaluation depends on screening findings and facility protocol.
scope_exclusions.thickened_liquids_before_assessment: Not endorsed. A modified liquid consistency is not assumed safe before swallowing status is assessed.
scope_exclusions.time_critical_oral_medication_exception: Not tested. If a medication is urgent, the care team should determine a safe nonoral alternative or individualized plan rather than bypass swallowing-safety assessment.

near_duplicate_check.note: V2-Q0724 tests rapid-response escalation for postoperative deterioration. V2-Q0677 tests active seizure safety. V2-Q0776 tests sterile-field contamination. V2-Q0821 tests prevention of oral-intake aspiration after acute stroke while dysphagia screening is pending. Targeted repository search for aspiration/dysphagia/swallowing precautions returned no matching item before staging.

option_audit.A: Plausible bedside swallow observation but uses oral water before the approved screening process and may miss silent aspiration.
option_audit.B: Correct. It prevents oral exposure until swallowing safety is evaluated through the approved process.
option_audit.C: Plausible texture modification but assumes thickened liquid is safe before dysphagia assessment.
option_audit.D: Plausible medication-timing response but oral medications in applesauce still require safe swallowing ability.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible best answer. The stem establishes acute stroke and an incomplete facility-approved dysphagia screen. B alone avoids all oral intake until swallowing safety is assessed. A/C/D each introduce oral material before that assessment.

cueing_check.note: Exact character counts were calculated from the stored strings. All four options are within six characters; correct option B is neither shortest nor longest.
